boxAlignment.question: Do the editor's boxes lie on what they mark?

observedBefore.what: in the 2026-10-05 runs the boxes lay off what they marked on every screen but a 4:3 one, scaled about the view's centre: in q3dm17 at 1600x900 the ammo_rockets box a third farther from the centre than its model, the trigger_teleport box beside the teleporter; farther at 2560x1080; matching at 1024x768

boxAlignment.cause: CL_EntityEditorAdjustView projected the overlay with the view the client hands the renderer, and every renderer then widens a 4:3-authored field of view for the screen's shape inside RE_RenderScene (R_ApplyProfileFovCorrection, code/renderercommon/tr_q3_fov.h; r_fovCorrection 1 by default in every profile but q3test, q3-ihv and jk2): 90 by 58.72 degrees at 16:9 drawn at 106.26 by 73.74, so the overlay was scaled by the tangents' ratio, 4/3 at 16:9 and 1.78 at 2560x1080; picking used the same projection; a view the editor widened (ET's limbo camera) was widened again by the renderer

fix.fieldOfView: the editor's own, cl_entityEditorFov (default 90, range 10-140, CVAR_ARCHIVE_ND) across a 4:3 screen, its height kept on others (ee::FitFieldOfView), the displayed shape (glconfig.windowAspect; the render's own with r_renderScale 2 or 4), flagged RDF_NOFOVCORRECTION on every view the editor draws so the renderer draws it as given; the overlay projects with the same view

observations: Every installed map's entity lump (607 maps, 12 titles) parses, keeps its worldspawn first, holds no token past 1,023 bytes, and is reproduced byte for byte by the editor's writer.
q3dm17's override written by sv_saveentfile and by the editor equals the retail BSP lump byte for byte (SHA-256 3063891b17639c53...).
After Apply, the q3 game spawned a weapon_bfg that q3dm17's BSP does not hold, and the player picked it up.

Each of the eleven profiles probed on a local server loaded the saved override on both of its restarts, by the server's own log line; on the Quake III line the structural Apply loaded the map again and the value-only Apply used map_restart 0.
A malformed override is set aside with its line and reason, and the BSP's entities run.
A jka-mp client of a dedicated fnTech3 server with sv_cheats 1 opened the editor, made an entity and saved maps/mp/ffa1.ent; Apply was refused for a server outside the process.

RTCW SP's retail cgame hung after map_restart 0 in 3 of 6 full runs when the entity list had changed, in none of 6 for a value-only change or a reload, and in none of 8 after the rule and none of 6 on the final build.
Q3Test 1.02 to 1.05 hold no map_restart string in their engine or game module; 1.06 to 1.08 do.

On dedicated servers, the q3-ihv, jk2-mp and jka-mp game modules and jka-sp's Init reported an override's marker entity as having no spawn function, and did not with sv_entityOverrides 0; jk2-sp stopped at client import 3 before choosing any entity text.

A Linux i686 dedicated server wrote q3dm17's entities byte for byte as the Windows server does (SHA-256 3063891b17639c53...), loaded the override with a marker entity, and Quake III's QVM game module reported the marker; the sv_entityOverrides 0 control did neither.

Over hm_voy1's 1,041 entities seen from above with every label on, the first overlay bounds overflowed the renderer's command buffer and the panels were dropped; with the budget and the Dear ImGui interface the same view drew 48 boxes and 286 dots in 2,423 commands, about 209 of 320 KiB, nothing left out, and mp_beach's 871 entities 48 boxes and 251 dots in 2,700 commands, about 229 KiB.
Enemy Territory's client game drew snow from an atmosphere key only oasis's override carried (742 near-white pixels in the view against a control's 195), so its entity tokens followed the override.
Quake III's probe passed at 1024x768, 1280x720 and 2560x1080 as well as 1600x900.

2026-10-06: the editor's boxes lay off what they marked by the renderers' field-of-view correction on every screen but 4:3; with the editor's own field drawn as given they lie on the ammunition, the teleporter and the lights in Quake III's captures at 1600x900, 2560x1080 and 1024x768 under GLx, Vulkan and RTX (boxAlignment).
inferences: jk2-sp, which stops before its game module initialises, would receive the override through the same selector and Init text the source tests pin; the editor cannot run in q3-ihv, jka-sp, jk2-sp or jk2-mp, whose clients cannot yet run a level here (the IHV client is blocked, the Jedi SP clients' admission is open, and jk2-mp's client game refuses renderer imports).
The RTCW SP hang comes from client game state that map_restart keeps per entity number (see rtcwSpRestart).

2026-10-06: Ritual's and 2015's model entities other than items, players and path nodes stand on their origins as those do; the editor reads no model to confirm a given one's box. Medal of Honor's model detail and Enemy Territory's foliage distance, judged by the field a game gave before the renderers widen it (fovXAuthored), judge the editor's flagged view by its widened field, so on a wide screen they may draw a little coarser in the editor than in play; not measured (boxAlignment).
openItems: jka-mp: Apply works over rcon, but the jka-mp client cannot yet host a listen server (its cgame's bolt queries need the remote-client frame clock; local-server clock sharing is not served) nor follow any server map change (its Ghoul2 renderer's attachment boundary), so after an Apply it must reconnect; both are limits of that profile, met without the editor too.

q3-ihv, jka-sp, jk2-sp and jk2-mp have no editor run: their clients stop before any level (clientStartupStops; the IHV client is blocked by its profile); jk2-sp has no override run either (see inferences).

Jedi Academy's client-side entity text following a local override needs the listen server its client cannot yet host; Enemy Territory's and RTCW multiplayer's are shown (clientEntityTokens, rtcwClientEntityTokens).
